The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Venkatarayappa, in the road traffic accident that took place on 19.07.2022.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 19.07.2022 at about 8.55 a.m., when deceased Venkatarayappa was crossing the road on BB Main Road, near Coffee Day, Yelahanka, Bangalore that time the driver of Bolero jeep, bearing Reg.No.KA-43-G-0167 came from Rajajnakunte to Yelahanka side, driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life and dashed to deceased.
Due to impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to the fatal injuries on the spot.

It Eramma vs K.G.I.D on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69018930/
2 is contended that, post-mortem was conducted at Yelahanka Government hospital and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.

sentences.text: It is stated that the deceased was working as Agricultural (Coolie) and earning Rs.800/- per day.
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No. KA-43-G-0167.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
3. On service of notice, respondent No.1 to 3 have entered appearance through their respective learned counsels.
The respondent No.1 to 3 have filed objection statements.
4. The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased and also the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It has denied that the Bolero Jeep, bearing Reg.No.KA-43-G-0167 was involved in accident did not have a valid insurance on date of accident.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has denied the age,
income and occupation of the deceased and also the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It has admitted the insurance was in force as on the date of the accident and insurance policy is valid as on the date of accident and covers the risk.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.
6. The 3rd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has stated that there was no nexus between the death of Venkataramappa and the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-13-F-2412,
in this context this respondent stated that oblique reasons the driver of the Bolero Jeep who hand in glove with the claimants falsely implicated the KSRTC bus in the accident in which the deceased died due to the injuries sustained by him when he was crossing the road due to hit by the Bolero Jeep subsequently and foisted a false case with the help of the police with the sole intention to make an unlawful gain from the KSRTC and further expecting that it would be easy to get compensation from the KSRTC.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased and also the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.

Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of Eramma vs K.G.I.D on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69018930/
3 the petition.

7. Based on the pleadings, this tribunal has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 19.07.2022 at about 8.55 a.m., when the deceased was crossing the road on BB Main road, near Coffee day, Yelahanka,
Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the Bolero Jeep, bearing Reg.No.KA-43-G-0167 by driving the same in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the deceased. Due to the impact deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or Award?
8.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P1 to 14.
On the other hand, respondent No.3/Driver is examined as RW.1 and got marked 3 documents as per Ex.R1 to R3 and closed its side.

9. Heard the arguments and perused the written arguments of Respondent No.2 and also records.
10.

The learned counsel for respondent No.3 has relied upon the following decisions:
1. (2014) 13 SCC 254 in between Lachod Ram and others V/s. Himachal Road Transport corporation.
2. MFA 2829/2009 (MV) in between Manju V/s. Mathue K.P. and others.
3.Civil Appeal No.10145/2019 in between Nishan Singh and Ors. V/s. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., and Ors.
4. (2005) 6 SCC 172 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Prembai Patel and others.
5. (2007) 5 SCC 428 in between Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Meena Variyal and others.
6. (2007) 13 SCC 476 in between Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Premlata Shukla and others.
11. My findings on the above issues as under:-

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1: It is the case of the petitioners that, on 19.07.2022 at about 8.55 a.m., when deceased Venkatarayappa was crossing the road on B.B. Main Road, near Coffee Day, Yelahanka,
Bangalore, that time the driver of Bolero jeep, bearing Reg.No.KA-43-G-0167 came from Rajajnakunte to Yelahanka side, driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life and dashed to deceased.
Due to impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to the fatal injuries on the spot

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the Bolero jeep driver and as such the respondents No.1 and 2 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

After filing of the written statement by the Respondent No.2, petitioner counsel has filed the impleading application for implead the KSRTC as proposed 3 rd Respondent, the said application allowed and made them as 3rd Respondent.
Thereafter, petitioner has not sought any relief against the 3rd Respondent except made him has party to the petition.

13. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 herself stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot Panchanama, IMV report, Charge sheet, Post Mortem Report, Inquest report and witness statement as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
14.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of Bolero Jeep, bearing Reg.No.KA-43-G-0167.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

Eramma vs K.G.I.D on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69018930/
5
Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

15. According to the version of petitioners, the accident happened near Coffee Day, Yelahanka,
Bengaluru, at about 8.55 a.m when deceased Venkatarayappa was crossing the road on BB Main Road, at that time the driver of Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-43-G-0167 came from Devanahalli towards Bengaluru, drove it in high speed, rash and negligent manner endangering human life and dashed to deceased.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.

The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P3 being the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P4 is the sketch prepared at the time of spot mahazar which reflects that deceased was crossing the road and suddenly the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased.
If the driver of Bolero Jeep vehicle had come in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicle and the pedestrians who was crossing the road, he could avoid the accident.
Further as per sketch and spot mahazar the accident occurred on side of the road divider and it clears that deceased was almost near to crossing the road.
If driver of Bolero Jeep has taken little care and precautions he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more, the contents of Ex.P5 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.

16. On the other hand, respondent No.1 has contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence of deceased himself who was crossing the road without observing the on going vehicles on the highway road and also driver of the KSRTC bus made the deceased to alight from the bus which was not the place of bus stop in a negligent manner.
The driver of the KSRTC bus also one of the accused as per police chargesheet.
But the respondent No.1 has not stepped into the witness box in order to prove the same.

The Respondent No.3 has examined the driver of the Bus as RW.1 and got marked log sheet, out register extract, ticket details schedule at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3 and also submits that the deceased has not travelled in their bus on the date of accident.
Even the Respondent No.1 or the petitioner has not examined the eye witness of the accident to prove that after alighting from the KSRTC bus deceased was crossing the road.

On perusal of the Ex.P2 which is the complaint given by one Shrinath who is the police constable, in which it stated that after verifying the pocket of deceased they found bus ticket and on the basis of bus ticket they assumed that the deceased was crossing the road after alighting from the KSRTC bus.
But in the petition there are no supporting documents or oral evidence to prove the negligence of the bus driver.

17. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered Eramma vs K.G.I.D on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69018930/
6 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the the instant case the driver of the Bolero Jeep is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even Respondent No.1 and 2 have not examined the eye witnesses of the accident to show the driver of KSRTC bus has made the deceased to alight from the bus on the highway road and after alighting from the bus deceased was crossing the road.

As already observed,
this court has clearly opined that the accident occurred due to the fault of the driver of the Bolero Jeep.

18. Further though PW.1 was cross examined by respondent counsel at length, nothing is elicited from her mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of deceased and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3 to P5 coupled with Ex.P6 clearly demonstrated that there is negligence on the part of offending vehicle Jeep driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-43-G- 0167 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that accident has taken place due to the rash and negligence of driver of the Bolero Jeep, bearing Reg.No.KA-43-G- 0167.
The petitioners claim that, Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the son of deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
Aadhar cards of petitioners marked at Ex's.P.13 and 14 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.

Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
Eramma vs K.G.I.D on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69018930/
7 20.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was working as Agricultural/Coolie and earning Rs.800/- per day.
In order to prove the same, petitioners have not produced any documents before the court.
Therefore, considering the occupation of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- per month.
21. It is stated that the deceased was aged years at the time of the accident.
The petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P12 which shows the year of birth as 1962.
The accident was occurred on 19.07.2022.
Hence the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 60 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '9'.
22.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 60 years.
Therefore, in this case, 10% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Hence, if 10% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.17,050/-p.m. (Rs.15,500/-
+ 1,550/-).
The deceased died leaving behind 2 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.11,367/- p.m.(Rs.17,050 - Rs.5,683).
23.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,367/- p.m. and the multiplier '9' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.12,27,636/- (Rs.11,367X 12 X 9).
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.12,27,636/- under the head of loss of dependency.

24. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
25.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 son of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 is entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children Eramma vs K.G.I.D on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69018930/
8 and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father,
Therefore, petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.44,000/- under the head of Filial consortium.

26. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency 12,27,636/-
2. Towards loss of Consortium to 44,000/-
the petitioner No.1 3. Towards loss to estate 16,500/-
4. Towards transportation of dead 16,500/-
body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 5.

Towards loss of Filial 44,000/-
 consortium to petitioner No.2 to  Rs.44,000/-)
 Total 13,48,636/-
In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.13,48,636/-.
27.
As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1 st petitioner is the widow, petitioners No.2 is the son of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No.1 and are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 70:30.
28.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondents have denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.

Eramma vs K.G.I.D on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69018930/
9 29.
Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Bolero vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-43-G-0167.
It is not in dispute that 2 nd respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of vehicle KA-43-G-0167 and the insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident and it covers the risk.

Further, on persual of unmarked insurance policy issued in respect of vehicle KA-43-G- 0167 it reflects that the insurance policy was issued from 29.06.2022 to 28.06.2023 and the accident occurred on 19.07.2022, therefore it clears that insurance policy was valid on the date of accident.
The respondents No.1 and 2 have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 1st respondent shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petition is dismissed against the Respondent No.3 .

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.13,48,636/-(Rupees Thirteen lakhs forty eight thousand six hundred and thirty six only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 70% Petitioner No.2 - 30% Further it is ordered that, 25% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioner No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years in her name and remaining 75% of the amount is ordered to be released in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share amount apportioned in the name of petitioners No.2 is ordered to be released in their favour respectively through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1: It is the case of the petitioners that, on 19.07.2022 at about 8.55 a.m., when deceased Venkatarayappa was crossing the road on B.B. Main Road, near Coffee Day, Yelahanka,
Bangalore, that time the driver of Bolero jeep, bearing Reg.No.KA-43-G-0167 came from Rajajnakunte to Yelahanka side, driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life and dashed to deceased.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
16. On the other hand, respondent No.1 has contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence of deceased himself who was crossing the road without observing the on going vehicles on the highway road and also driver of the KSRTC bus made the deceased to alight from the bus which was not the place of bus stop in a negligent manner.
On perusal of the Ex.P2 which is the complaint given by one Shrinath who is the police constable, in which it stated that after verifying the pocket of deceased they found bus ticket and on the basis of bus ticket they assumed that the deceased was crossing the road after alighting from the KSRTC bus.
But in the petition there are no supporting documents or oral evidence to prove the negligence of the bus driver.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.12,27,636/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.

Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
Hence, 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 1st respondent shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petition is dismissed against the Respondent No.3 .
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.13,48,636/-(Rupees Thirteen lakhs forty eight thousand six hundred and thirty six only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 70% Petitioner No.2 - 30% Further it is ordered that, 25% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioner No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years in her name and remaining 75% of the amount is ordered to be released in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share amount apportioned in the name of petitioners No.2 is ordered to be released in their favour respectively through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
